'''Nikolay Serafimovich Zefirov''' (September 13, 1935 – April 28, 2017) - was a Russian chemist known for his research in [[Organic chemistry]] and [[Medicinal chemistry]] and the development of new synthetic methods.

== Academic career ==
Nikolai Zefirov was born in [[Yaroslavl]], [[Russia]], September 13, 1935.

He entered the [[Moscow State University]] Moscow State University in 1953 and began his research during his  [[Bachelor's degree]]. Zefirov joined Yury Yuriev's research group at the laboratory of [[heterocyclic compound]]s. His first article was published in Russian Journal of General Chemistry in 1956 and was dedicated to the preparation and applications of silicon [[carboxylate]]s. Nikolay Zefirov completed his [[MSc]] with honors in 1958, defending a [[thesis]] on "''Reactions of diene synthesis in the furan series''". Then he continued working as [[assistant professor]] in [[MSU Faculty of Chemistry]] and graduated his [[PhD|Ph.D]] "''New substitutive addition reactions in the furan series''" in 1961.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.chem.msu.ru/rus/history/acad/zefirov-75.pdf |title=Академик Николай С. Зефиров |date=13 September 2010 |website=Lomonosov MSU }}</ref>  [[File:Zefirov-thesis.tif|center|360px]]

His research was focused on [[Bicyclic molecule|bridged]] [[oxirane]]s which are capable undergoing the [[Wagner–Meerwein rearrangement]] in reaction with [[acetic anhydride]]. Later these transformations have found applications for the ''trans''-[[Jasmone]] synthesis. It is noteworthy that all research work of this time was conducted without access to NMR.
[[File:Zefirov-jasmone.jpg|center|380x380px]]
Zefirov obtained his [[habilitation]] in 1966. In 1970-1971 he interned at [[Princeton University]] in the [[USA]] as a [[Visiting Researcher]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://findingaids.princeton.edu/catalog/AC107-03_c7656 |title=Professional Staff files, Subgroup 3: C |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=30 June 1971 |website=Princeton University Library |publisher=Princeton University}}</ref> Upon his return in 1971, he became the Head of the [[Heterocyclic compound]]s laboratory. Ten years later, in 1981, he was appointed a [[Full Professor]] of [[Moscow State University]], [[MSU Faculty of Chemistry|the Department of Chemistry]]. In 1981, he also was elected a [[Corresponding Members|Corresponding Member]] of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] and in 1987 he became a Full Member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] referred to as [[Academician]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.chem.msu.ru/rus/history/acad/zefirov.html |title= Aкадемик Зефиров Николай Серафимович |date=13 September 2010 |website=Lomonosov MSU }}</ref>

He was founder and Head of the Laboratory of [[Mathematical chemistry]] and Computer Synthesis, Zelinsky Institute of Organic Chemistry (ZIOC RAS), Chief Scientific Director of the Institute of Physiologically Active Substances of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] (IPAC RAS), and Chief Researcher of the IPAC RAS.

He headed the [[Organic chemistry]] department, [[MSU Faculty of Chemistry]] (1994-2014). In 2015, he founded and headed the [[Medicinal chemistry|Medicinal Chemistry]] and Fine Organic Synthesis Department (2015-2017). Zefirov not only excelled as a scientist but also imparted knowledge to students through courses such as "Organic Synthesis", "Molecular Orbitals theory in Organic Chemistry", "Computer Molecular Modeling and QSAR". He has also been instrumental in launching the MSc [[Medicinal chemistry]] program at Moscow State University.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Palyulin | first1 = V.A. | year = 2004 | title = A Tribute to Prof. Nikolai Zefirov | journal = Arkivoc | volume = 2005 | issue = 4| pages = 1–7 | doi = 10.3998/ark.5550190.0006.401 | hdl = 2027/spo.5550190.0006.401 | hdl-access = free }}</ref>

Zefirov has authored over 1500 scientific articles and 94 patents.

== Major contributions ==

=== Synthetic organic chemistry ===

==== New approaches in Ad<sub>E</sub>-reactions ====
Zefirov made significant contributions to the understanding of [[Electrophilic addition]] reactions by establishing the [[ion-pair]] [[Reaction mechanism|mechanism]] using the example of [[Thiirane]] cations. In 1974 he discovered the phenomenon of increasing the effective electrophilicity of weak electrophiles, which was called "''Doping-addition''". Such effect occurs for weak [[electrophile]]s, increasing [[electrophilicity]] and making them reactive enough for  [[electrophilic addition]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zefirov | first1 = N.S. | display-authors = etal   | year = 1975 | title = New method for increasing of electrophilicity of weak electrophiles in addition reactions : Wagner-Meerwein rearrangement in a reaction of 2,4-dinitrobenzenesulfenyl chloride with norbornene | journal = Tetrahedron | volume = 31 | issue = 23| pages = 2948–2951 | doi = 10.1016/0040-4020(75)80317-6 }}</ref> Additionally Zefirov has developed thio[[acylation]] and thio[[amidation]] reactions in the presence of [[lithium perchlorate]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zefirov | first1 = N.S. | display-authors = etal   | year = 1985 | title = Kinetics and mechanism of the doping-addition of Arscl to olefins | journal = Tetrahedron | volume = 41 | issue = 22| pages = 5219–5227 | doi = 10.1016/S0040-4020(01)96771-7 }}</ref> The proposed reaction pathway includes [[onium ion]] formation with the following [[perchlorate]] ion addition. The “''doping effect''” can also be observed in more complex cases, such as induction of the skeletal  [[rearrangement reaction]] in [[Bicyclic molecule|bicyclic compounds]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zefirov | first1 = N.S. | display-authors = etal   | year = 1978 | title = Molecular structures of 8-hydroxy-9-carbomethoxy−4-(2-nitrophenyltio)-tetracyclo[4,2,2,02,5,03,7] decane-10-carboxylic acid lactone | journal = Tetrahedron | volume = 19 | issue = 29| pages = 2617–2620 | doi = 10.1016/S0040-4039(01)94844-0 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zefirov | first1 = N.S. | display-authors = etal   | year = 1979 | title = Doping-addition of arylsulfenyl chlorides to the tricyclo&#91;4,2,2,02,5&#93;deca-3,7,9-triene system: Skeletal rearrangements and serendipitious products | journal = Tetrahedron Lett. | volume = 20 | issue = 37| pages = 3533–3536 | doi = 10.1016/S0040-4039(01)95454-1 }}</ref> Zefirov is also known for the work on the [[Stereoselectivity|stereocontrol]] in reactions proceeding through the [[ion-pair]] mechanism.[[File:Zefirov-thiolation.jpg|center|360px]]

==== Nucleophilic properties of nucleofuge anions ====
Zefirov's research on the impact of LiClO<sub>4</sub> on [[electrophilic addition]] and [[nucleophilic substitution]] resulted in the revelation of the [[Nucleophile|Nucleophilic]]  characteristics of extremely weakly [[Nucleophile|nucleophilic]] [[anion]] like [[triflate]] and [[perchlorate]]. It has been shown that weak nucleophiles such can react through competitive covalent binding.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zefirov | first1 = N.S. | display-authors = etal   | year = 1985 | title = Oxidatively assisted nucleophilic substitution of iodine in alkyl iodides by nucleofugic anions | journal = J. Org. Chem. | volume = 50 | issue = 11| pages = 1872–1876 | doi = 10.1021/jo00211a017 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zefirov | first1 = N.S. | display-authors = etal   | year = 1985 | title = Competitive binding of nucleofugal anions in carbocationic-like processes | journal = Acc. Chem. Res. | volume = 18 | issue = 5| pages = 154–158 | doi = 10.1021/ar00113a005 }}</ref> Ultimately, this research led to the advancement of SO<sub>3</sub>-promoted [[Electrophilic addition|Ad<sub>E</sub>-reactions]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zefirov | first1 = N.S. | display-authors = etal   | year = 1984 | title = Chlorine chlorosulfate: synthesis and addition reactions with olefins | journal = J. Org. Chem. | volume = 49 | issue = 21| pages = 4086–4087 | doi = 10.1021/jo00195a050 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zefirov |first1=N.S. |last2=Zyk |first2=N.V. |display-authors=etal |year=1985 |title=Sulfur trioxide assisted electrophilic addition of R2NCl to olefins |journal=J. Org. Chem. |volume=50 |issue=23 |pages=4539–4543 |doi=10.1021/jo00223a022}}</ref>

==== Novel hypervalent reagents: I<sup>+3</sup>, Xe<sup>+2</sup>, Se<sup>+4</sup>, Te<sup>+4</sup> ====
He developed a novel class of hypervalent compounds and discovered their potential for use in fine [[organic synthesis]]. These compounds were identified as excellent reagents for [[oxidation reaction]]s. Moreover, their ability to exhibit strong [[electrophile]]s properties and serve as efficient [[leaving group]]s was investigated.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Yusubov |first1=M.S. |year=2021 |title=Zefirov's reagent and related hypervalent iodine triflates |journal=Mendeleev Commun. |volume=31 |issue=3 |pages=282–287 |doi=10.1016/j.mencom.2021.04.002|s2cid=236614544 }}</ref> Notably, one of the discovered compounds has been named Zefirov's reagent in honor of its discoverer. 
[[File:Zefirov's reagent.tif|center|130x130px]]

==== Spirocyclopropane structures ====
Zefirov was the pioneering chemist who conducted the synthesis of complex polycyclic structures, including heteroadamantanes. He also synthesized a novel class of spirocyclopropane structures and achieved the first successful synthesis of [[triangulane]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zefirov|first1=N.S. |display-authors=etal |year=1990 |title=Triangulanes: stereoisomerism and general method of synthesis |journal=J. Am. Chem. Soc. |volume=112 |issue=21 |pages=7707 |doi=10.1021/ja00177a034}}</ref> 
[[File:Zefirov-triangulanes.tif|center|360px]]

Amongst his studies on conformation, Zefirov found that spiro[2.5]octan-4-ol and derivatives thereof adopt predominantly axial conformations.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zefirov|first1=N.S. |display-authors=etal |year=1978 |title= New conformational effect: predominance of the axial conformation in spiro [5.2] octan-4-ol derivatives |journal=J. Chem. Soc., Chem. Commun. |volume=13 |issue=3 |pages=147-148 |doi=10.1039/C39780000147}}</ref> This effect was later shown by Izzotti and Gleason to extend to most functional groups, with particularly strong axial preferences for larger and more electronegative groups.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Izzotti|first1=A.R. |last2=Gleason|first2=J.L. |year=2024 |title= Driving tert-butyl axial: the surprising cyclopropyl effect |journal=Chem. Sci. |volume=15 |issue=44 |pages=18592-18600|doi=10.1039/d4sc05470a}}</ref>

==== Other ====
[[Tetranitromethane]] chemistry was among the scientific interests of N.S. Zefirov. It can react as a good [[dipole]] in [[1,3-Dipolar cycloaddition|1,3-dipolar cycloaddition]] with alkenes. It was found, that the reaction of [[Tetranitromethane|C(NO<sub>2</sub>)<sub>4</sub>]] with [[Α,β-Unsaturated carbonyl compound|a,β-Unsaturated carbonyl compound]] leads to [[isoxazole]] derivatives.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zefirov|first1=N.S. |display-authors=etal |year=2009 |title=Polynitromethanes - Unique Reagents in the Synthesis of Nitro-Substituted Heterocycles |journal=Synlett |volume=2009 |issue=10 |pages=1543–1557 |doi=10.1055/s-0029-1217190}}</ref>

Zefirov discovered several skeletal [[rearrangement reaction]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lukin|first1=K.A. |last2=Zefirov|first2=N.S. |display-authors=etal |year=1992 |title=Unusual rearrangement of triangulane gem-dibromides in the presence of methyllithium |journal=Tetrahedron |volume=48 |issue=45 |pages=9977–9984 |doi=10.1016/S0040-4020(01)92287-2}}</ref> He was involved in investigation of various theoretical organic chemistry problems, such as σ-π [[Conjugation (organic chemistry)|conjugation]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gribanova|first1=T.N. |last2=Zefirov|first2=N.S. |last3=Minkin|first3=V.I. |year=2010 |title=Structure and stability of the heteroannulated [8–10]circulenes: A quantum-chemical study |journal=Pure Appl. Chem. |volume=82 |issue=4 |pages=1011–1024 |doi=10.1351/PAC-CON-09-10-36|doi-access=free }}</ref> [[stereochemistry]], and [[conformational analysis]].<ref>{{cite journal  |last1=Zefirov|first1=N.S. |display-authors=etal |year=1976 |title=Stereochemical studies—XX: Conformations of 1,2-trans-disubstituted cyclohexanes |journal=Tetrahedron |volume=32 |issue=11 |pages=1211–1219 |doi=10.1016/0040-4020(76)80074-9}}</ref> He described the so-called “''hockey stick effect''” in conformationally mobile heterocyclic systems, and developed the Zefirov-Palulin model for calculation of folding parameters to describe the shape of cycles.<ref>{{cite journal  |last1=Zefirov|first1=N.S. |year=1977 |title=Stereochemical studies—XXI: General equation of relationship between products ratio and conformational equilibrium |journal=Tetrahedron |volume=33 |issue=20 |pages=2719–2722 |doi=10.1016/0040-4020(77)80296-2}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal  |last1=Zefirov|first1=N.S. |last2=Palulin|first2=V.A. |last3=Dashevskaya|first3=E.E.|year=1990 |title=Stereochemical studies. XXXIV†. Quantitative description of ring puckering via torsional angles. The case of six-membered rings |journal=Tetrahedron |volume=3  |pages=147 |doi=10.1002/poc.610030304}}</ref>

=== Computational chemistry ===
Zefirov is considered a pioneer in [[computational chemistry]] in Russia, having made significant contributions to the field. He developed a formal logical approach for the classification of organic reactions, as well as for the search new reactions and development of computer synthesis methods. Zefirov actively promoted [[QSAR]] in modern medicinal chemistry. His research spanned a wide range of topics within general organic chemistry problems, including the description of organic structures and reaction, the search for new structures, and the investigation of structure-activity correlations. Furthermore, he also conducted research on new drug-like compounds.<ref>{{cite journal  |last1=Zefirov|first1=N.S. |last2=Palulin|first2=V.A. |year=2002 |title=Fragmental Approach in QSPR |journal=J. Chem. Inf. Comput. Sci. |volume=42 |issue=5  |pages=1112–1122 |doi=10.1021/ci020010e|pmid=12376998 }}</ref>
